svg.text: The content generator - a complete agent on its own
Three skills, an agentic writer with a deterministic floor, and its own storage. Migration is one consumer of its output - not the owner of it.
content.ideate
"what should we write today?" - picks a
fresh on-lane topic when a run arrives with
no topic (this is what the daily loop leans on)
the lane + voice come from the caller, not from here
content.brief
a structured editorial brief: headline, dek,
sections of real multi-paragraph prose,
in-body links, target EDS blocks
the Brief shape IS the contract artifact
content.synthesize-source
renders a brief into a standalone "legacy"
HTML page (clean | dated | messy) plus a
groundTruth object for honest fidelity scoring
the raw material the closed loop migrates
The writer - agentic ceiling, deterministic floor (:4002, no browser, CPU-only)
Agentic tier - Claude Agent SDK
real editorial writing: compelling headlines, multi-paragraph prose, a dek, links - tool-free, timeout-bounded
creds-gated per call (OAuth token or API key present → agentic); tolerant JSON extraction on the way back
the site's voice arrives as data - the coordinator threads the site profile's siteBrief in; this agent has no hardcoded identity
any error → fall back - generation never breaks the loop
Deterministic floor - the template tier
coherent topic-substituted prose (never lorem), typed FeatureBlocks - stats · callout · quote · table · cta -
so migration gets distinct semantic blocks to map to EDS; a real scenic hero-image pool
$0, credential-free, always works - this is what CI and the fast e2e tier run on
both tiers return the same Brief / SyntheticSource shapes - callers can't tell which wrote it except by the working-note that says so
Its own storage
the store - tasks + artifacts rows
its own SQLite file locally; the shared
D1 database in the cloud - every task
persisted, restart- and sleep-tolerant
the bytes - R2 artifact store
sources/<taskId>.html → r2.dev
a PUBLIC URL on purpose: Make.com,
Kimi-in-a-container, and eval all fetch
it over plain HTTP
the URL is the handoff; the row is the index
Fully functional without the rest of the mesh
Its own Agent Card, its own edge shim (POST /hooks/content-gen/<skill>), its own store. Nothing in this agent knows about EDS or migration.
Point a different consumer at it and it's a research / content-generation agent for any pipeline: ideate → brief → publish the brief itself as the product.
consumers today: the migration stage (closed loop) · the daily loop's ideation · you, over curl - consumers tomorrow: a weekly research digest, a newsletter, another mesh
Decoupling test: could this agent move to a different repo, a different team, a different company - and keep working? Yes: callers hold only its URL and its contract.
Resilience rule: the agentic tier can time out, return garbage, or have no credentials - the deterministic floor answers anyway. A red generate stage always means something else.
